name: Science Question Answering (ScienceQA)
description: A large-scale multimodal multiple choice science question answering dataset consisting of 21,208 examples with diverse science topics and annotations of their answers with corresponding lectures and explanations. The dataset covers three subjects (natural science, social science, and language science) across grades 1-12, featuring questions with multimodal contexts (text and images) to support multi-hop reasoning and chain-of-thought explanation generation.

creator.name: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
creator.affiliation: University of California Los Angeles, Arizona State University, Allen Institute for AI

citeAs: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan. Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. NeurIPS 2022.
rai:dataCollection: Questions in the ScienceQA dataset are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education. The dataset includes problems that align with California Common Core Content Standards. The original science problems were downloaded and then individual components (e.g. questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted based on heuristic rules.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in K-12 education, aligned with California Common Core Content Standards.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Invalid questions were manually removed, such as questions that have only one choice, questions that contain faulty data, and questions that are duplicated. If there were multiple correct answers that applied, only one correct answer was kept. Answer options of each question were shuffled to ensure the choices do not follow any specific pattern. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat the lectures and solutions to make special structures in the texts (such as tables and lists) easily distinguishable from simple text passages.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted from original science problems based on heuristic rules. Invalid questions were manually removed. Answer options were shuffled. Lectures and solutions were reformatted using semi-automated scripts. A data exploration tool was developed to review examples in the collected dataset, and incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Most questions (83.9%) are annotated with lectures that provide general external knowledge introducing background information for solving problems of a similar class. 90.5% of questions feature explanations that reveal specific reasons for the answer. The lecture and explanation annotations were extracted from the original source materials and reformatted.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question has one correct answer. 83.9% of questions have a lecture annotation. 90.5% of questions have an explanation annotation.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Image captions were extracted using a captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 for use as visual context in language models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset does not contain any user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race. Due to the nature of data sources (textbooks), ScienceQA does not contain personally identifiable information.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The ScienceQA dataset is proposed to diagnose the multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems. It is beneficial to both follow-up research work and real-world applications, providing a useful benchmark for multi-modal learning, multi-hop reasoning, and general artificial intelligence. ScienceQA will contribute to the development of K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems.
rai:dataLimitations: Current multimodal methods and large language models fail to achieve satisfactory performance on ScienceQA. Failure cases can be classified into two types: (a) the model fails to understand the multimodal inputs and lacks domain-specific knowledge to arrive at the correct answer; (b) the model generates the wrong chain of thought with irrelevant, incorrect, or incomplete information. Image captions lack fine-grained semantics and usually do not work well for diagrams. Large language models face challenges reasoning about questions that require understanding complex and uncommon domain knowledge.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is split into training (60%), validation (20%), and test (20%) sets for model training, development, and evaluation. Use cases include: Training and fine-tuning models for multimodal question answering, testing multi-hop reasoning abilities, evaluating chain-of-thought explanation generation, and benchmarking visual question answering systems. The dataset is available for non-commercial research purposes only.
